title: The Internet Connections and Services
part: Part D — Networks and the Internet

blocks.html: After studying this chapter you will be able to:

items.html: describe the structure of the internet and the role of ISPs

explain who manages the internet and what net neutrality means
describe the growth of the internet in India and future trends

blocks.html: The internet is a global network of networks that communicate using the TCP/IP protocols. No single company or country owns it. Thousands of networks — owned by telecom companies, universities, governments and businesses — agree to connect and exchange traffic.

blocks.caption: Figure 14.1 · How a home connects to the global internet

blocks.html: An ISP is a company that provides internet access to homes, schools and businesses, usually for a monthly fee. Indian ISPs include BSNL, Jio, Airtel, Vi, ACT Fibernet and many local cable operators.

rows: Very large carriers that own international and undersea cables and connect to each other without paying
National or regional providers that buy some access from Tier 1 and connect to others
Local providers that sell connections directly to homes and offices

blocks.html: Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) are places where many networks connect directly to exchange traffic locally. In India, NIXI (National Internet Exchange of India) runs exchanges so that Indian traffic stays within India, making it faster and cheaper.

rows: Very slow; phone busy while online; obsolete
Carried digital voice and data together; now outdated
A few Mbps to about 100 Mbps (VDSL)
Always on; phone can be used at the same time
Shared with neighbours; speed may drop at busy times
Very fast and reliable; growing quickly in India
Guaranteed, symmetric speed; costly; used by offices and banks
4G: tens of Mbps; 5G: hundreds of Mbps
Internet anywhere; data limits; speed depends on signal
Wireless from a router or phone

items.html: ADSL (Asymmetric DSL) — download faster than upload; suits homes.
SDSL (Symmetric DSL) — equal upload and download; suits offices.
VDSL (Very-high-bit-rate DSL) — the fastest DSL over short distances.

rows: Download and upload speed in Mbps; online classes and video calls need good upload too
Monthly data allowance; speed after the limit (Fair Usage Policy)
Monthly or yearly cost; installation charges
How often the connection fails; ask neighbours
Important for video calls and games
Availability in your area; how quickly faults are repaired

blocks.html: Worked example: A family uses about 4 GB a day on video classes and streaming. In a 30- day month that is 4 × 30 = 120 GB, so a plan with only 100 GB per month will run out before the month ends.

rows: Real-time text, voice notes, group chats
Voice and video calls over the internet; online classes and meetings
Uploading and downloading files; cloud links for large files
Online courses, recorded lectures, quizzes (SWAYAM, DIKSHA)
Government services online (DigiLocker, UMANG, land records)
Storing files and using software online (SaaS, storage, cloud servers)
Smart meters, cameras, appliances and sensors connected to the internet
Part of an intranet opened to selected outsiders
Example: a supplier portal of a car company

blocks.html: The internet works through cooperation among many organisations:

rows: Coordinates domain names and IP address allocation worldwide
Develops internet standards such as TCP/IP
Develops web standards such as HTML and CSS
Hand out IP addresses (APNIC serves the Asia-Pacific region)
In India: Department of Telecommunications (DoT), TRAI (telecom regulator), NIXI (.in domains and internet exchanges), MeitY (IT policy)

blocks.html: Net neutrality means that ISPs must treat all internet traffic equally — they should not block, slow down or charge differently for particular websites or apps. In 2016, TRAI banned discriminatory pricing of data based on content, and India adopted strong net- neutrality rules in 2018.

items.html: Public internet began on 15 August 1995 through VSNL.
Cheap smartphones and low-cost mobile data from 2016 onwards brought hundreds of millions of new users online.
BharatNet is laying optical fibre to connect gram panchayats.
Common Service Centres provide digital services in villages.
5G services began in India in October 2022.
India has one of the largest internet user bases in the world, and most Indians access the internet mainly through mobile phones.
5G and 6G for very high speed and very low delay.
IoT in homes, farms and cities.
Satellite internet from low-orbit satellites for remote areas.
AI-powered services in Indian languages.
IPv6 to give every device its own address.
Verify information from more than one reliable source before believing or forwarding it.
Protect accounts with strong passwords and two-step verification.
Respect copyright; cite sources in school projects.
Balance screen time with sleep, exercise and offline activities.
Use the internet to learn — free courses, libraries and tutorials are a great opportunity.

blocks.html: Did you know? More than 95% of international internet traffic travels through optical fibre cables laid on the ocean floor. Several such cables land at Mumbai and Chennai, connecting India to the rest of the world.
Aim: To study internet connections and services practically.

items.html: Your ISP. Find out the ISP, connection type and plan (speed, data limit, price) used at home and at school.
Speed test. Run a speed test on two connections; record download, upload and ping. Compare them with the plan.
Data use. On a phone, open Settings → Network → Data usage. List the five apps that used the most data in the last month.

Plan comparison. Collect three fibre plans and three mobile plans available in your area. Compare cost per GB and speed in an Excel table, and choose the best plan for a family of four. Justify your choice.
Services map. List 15 internet services your family uses and group them under the categories of Section 14.3.
The internet is a network of networks using TCP/IP; ISPs at Tier 1, 2 and 3 connect users, and IXPs (NIXI in India) exchange traffic locally.
Connection types: dial-up, ISDN, DSL (ADSL, SDSL, VDSL), cable, fibre (FTTH), leased line, mobile 4G/5G, Wi-Fi hotspot and satellite.
Choose a plan by speed, data limit, price, reliability, latency and support.
Internet services include the web, email, messaging, VoIP, FTP, e-learning, e- commerce, e-governance, social media, streaming, cloud and IoT.
ICANN, IETF and W3C coordinate the internet; TRAI, DoT, NIXI and MeitY handle India. Net neutrality means all traffic is treated equally.
India's internet grew rapidly through mobile data, BharatNet and 5G.
